title: Illegal Piggery Demolition in Co Cork Reveals Asbestos
text:
A recent unpermitted demolition in Grenagh , Co Cork, has unleashed an asbestos scare, raising serious health concerns for the community. This article details the unfolding incident, the official response from local authorities, adn the steps being taken to mitigate potential risks. Learn about the dangers of asbestos exposure and the measures in place to protect public health.
asbestos Scare Grips Grenagh After Unpermitted Demolition Grenagh, Co Cork — April 16, 2025
Key Takeaways cork County Council confirms asbestos presence at demolished farm building in Grenagh. Demolition occurred without necessary permits,raising public health concerns. risk mitigation measures are underway, including air monitoring and site dampening. The Incident Unfolds A former piggery in Grenagh, Co Cork, became the center of community concern after its unpermitted demolition revealed a hidden danger: asbestos.
Cork County Council was alerted to the situation April 13 after residents raised concerns about potential asbestos exposure from the demolished structure.
The demolition, which lacked proper authorization, triggered immediate action from local authorities.
Community Response and Safety Measures The community’s apprehension was palpable, leading to precautionary measures.
cancellation of GAA games on a nearby pitch. Closure of the local playground. These steps were taken due to fears that airborne materials from the rubble of the demolished could impact on people’s health.
Council and HSA Intervention Following the demolition, officials from Cork County Council’s environment and planning sections, along wiht the Health and Safety Authority (HSA), conducted an inspection.
The council confirmed that the demolition had taken place without permission.
A subsequent inspection by an environmental management expert confirmed the presence of asbestos on Wednesday.
Understanding Asbestos risks Asbestos, composed of long, thin fibers, poses meaningful health risks.
It is linked to severe diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma.
Its widespread use in building materials, particularly before 1999, means it remains a concern in older structures.
While now illegal to place on the market, asbestos persists in buildings constructed before the millennium.
The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) emphasizes that improper removal increases the risk of fibre inhalation.
Therefore, asbestos removal is a complex procedure which must onyl be done by a specialist contractor as asbestos waste is hazardous.
Risk Mitigation in Action Cork County Council is actively implementing measures to mitigate the risks associated with the asbestos exposure.
Air monitors are being set up at the site’s perimeters. Regular monitoring ensures no disturbance of the materials. Spraying of the material to dampen it and mitigate the risk of windblown particles. Continued Coordination Communication and collaboration are central to managing the situation.
cork County Council continues to correspond with the landowner on this matter in addition to the other agencies involved including the HSE, EPA and HSA.
Spokesperson for Cork County Council
Looking Ahead The incident underscores the importance of adhering to regulations regarding building demolitions and handling hazardous materials.
Ongoing monitoring and remediation efforts will be crucial to ensuring the long-term safety and well-being of the Grenagh community.
